rv.q: Fifty years ago, the marital revelations and commentary on gender roles as depicted in Art of Leaving might be considered titillating and risqué.

Unfortunately, wives who remain dishrags for their husband have gone out of style at least a generation ago and her hero is so obnoxious that we don’t understand why Diana put up with him for a quarter of a century.
Art of Leaving falls short of poignantly realizing the journey of a middle-aged wife leaving her cartoonishly undeserving husband.
There’s not much art here, but the desire to leave remains.
The Art of Leaving is playing a limited engagement now through December 14th at the Alice Griffin Jewel Box Theatre/Pershing Square Signature Center, 480 W. 42nd Street, NYC.
But even the sharpest direction couldn’t improve this script, as irredeemable as Aaron himself.

cn.t: Critics pan this dated comedy as an amateurish throwback to 1960s sitcom fare, with cardboard dialogue and emotionally abusive scenarios played for laughs that fall flat.
